observation: Planner disproved the work package's OWN stated cause. plan.md:9 and the source audit both said page bodies clip because they omit `min-h-0`; round.md §2.3 measured 7 layout shapes in headless Chromium and showed `min-h-0` on a scrolling body is a no-op (shapes A≡B) — an element whose overflow isn't `visible` already gets flex min-size 0, so `overflow-y-auto` supplies the reset by itself. The track's whole '30+ sites survive by luck' framing rested on an unmeasured CSS claim. Founder accepted the correction (round.md §7); it supersedes plan.md:9 and the audit.

Planner found a second genuinely-broken page the three-pass UI audit missed: `/artifacts/:id` (ArtifactPermalink.tsx, all 4 branches) has no page scaffold at all (shape E — no bounded root height, no scroll region), so a long artifact plus its discussion thread is unreachable. Caught by reading the source for the broken shape, not by re-running the audit's grep. round.md §2.4.

Planner caught that the audit's `overflow-y-auto` grep under-counted correct scroll regions: ReviewComposition.tsx:760 spells it `overflow-auto` and was missed, so plan.md's '4 regions declare the reset' was actually 5 (round.md §2.5). Consequence: the new lint rule had to match `overflow-auto` and `overflow-y-scroll`, not just `overflow-y-auto`, or it would have a blind spot on the very spelling that hid a region from the audit.

Reviewer's first e2e run failed 10/21 from cross-worktree contamination — nearly a false verdict. Playwright's `reuseExistingServer: !CI` is true locally and AZ2-page-scroll.spec.ts hard-codes `--strictPort 5179`; a stale idle vite from a SIBLING worktree (pipeline-az6-12697d, PID 94104) held 5179, so Playwright reused az6's pre-change code and the team/artifact AC tests ran against a build with no PageScaffold. Reviewer freed the port and re-ran with CI=1 (forces a fresh server from THIS worktree) → 21/21. A real, repeatable trap for any parallel pipeline run whose e2e lane shares a hard-coded strictPort. review.md L22-33, L106-115.

The cross-worktree contamination doubled as an accidental break-test proving the e2e spec is not a passenger: served the pre-PageScaffold code the team + `/artifacts/:id` AC tests went RED for the exact right reason (`scrollContainers:0`, `[data-page-scroll]` resolving to 0 elements — the original live defect); served the fixed code, green 21/21. Red/green discrimination proven on real Chromium, not asserted. review.md L18-33.

Line-count estimate off ~9x. round.md §6 risk 6 estimated ~550 changed lines under Fork A1 (component+stories ~120, migration ~180, lint+tests ~150, e2e ~120); real diff is 4888 insertions / 2927 deletions across 35 files (base 0341a11b..HEAD). The gap is JSX re-indentation: wrapping every page root+body in `<PageScaffold>` re-indents whole file bodies (review.md:58 confirms the ~2900 deletions are re-indentation), which the ~180 migration figure never costed. Estimate was behaviour-correct but magnitude-blind.

Abbreviated founder-approved procedure ran as specified: one combined refine+design+architecture artifact (round.md) -> one founder approval (concept gate, 2 forks decided) -> one build session (21 commits, 35 files) -> one fresh review round. Zero critique phases, zero separate refine/design/architecture phases, one human gate, no second gate after approval. Result: review returned DONE on the FIRST round, 0 blocking findings (4 non-blocking). No retries. Proportionate here — the cut ceremony did not cost quality, because the single planner measured instead of trusting and caught the wrong stated cause + two audit errors that critique phases would nominally have been the place to catch. Effort split: most of the ~7800 line-touches were mechanical re-indent migrating 15 pages onto PageScaffold to buy a flat lint prohibition; the actual user-facing defect was 2 pages / 'one class name'. That migration-heavy split was the deliberate Fork A1 trade, not drift.
